fields.question: Why test both attention and recurrence for bidirectional conversion?
fields.answer: Removing the attention mask can leave recurrence one-way. Local CUDA only confirms component execution, not a 9B checkpoint or full denoising curves.
fields.example: Right context reaching one branch does not make the other bidirectional.

fields.question: Why not use ECHO bonus logits as the final sampling distribution?
fields.answer: Frequent cheap early proposals and less frequent authoritative late checks cooperatively expand the candidate tree. Exploration may differ from the target and requires exact rejection correction. Local candidate/tensor checks do not measure throughput.
fields.example: A bonus branch may enter verification without being accepted automatically.

fields.question: Why explore frequently in early layers but verify less often at the end?
fields.answer: Early proposals are cheap; full depth verifies reliably. Dual loops and bonus logits expand candidates while aiming to reduce waits and preserve corrected sampling.
fields.example: Let the light path expand promising branches for full-depth checking.

fields.question: Why separate exploration scores from target sampling?
fields.answer: Bonus logits serve proposals and expansion. Exact rejection correction maintains the target distribution. Sampling bonuses directly changes behavior.
fields.example: Trying a favored candidate first does not entitle it to higher final probability.

fields.question: How does candidate merge validation differ from CUDA throughput evidence?
fields.answer: Reference verifies merge and lossless correction; A100 receipt verifies the tensor path. Real speed needs early/late scheduling, caching, and measured time.
fields.example: Distribution parity does not prove ideal GPU overlap.

fields.question: Why detach only the explicit codebook shortcut, not the entire noisy input?
fields.answer: Both paths share a codebook. Detaching shortcut gradient still lets the codebook learn through noisy input; detaching everything breaks it. Training uses entropy-gated self-conditioning while inference uses unweighted posterior mean.
fields.example: Freeze one shortcut multiplication, not the same table's input construction path.

fields.question: Why add a likelihood shortcut besides noisy embeddings?
fields.answer: Codebook-to-noisy-state relations supplement token posterior with noise-conditioned backbone and bounded calibration. This is more than a normal head and needs correct gradients and self-conditioning.
fields.example: At low noise, nearby codebook vectors help identify the underlying token.

fields.question: Should training entropy gating also weight inference posterior means?
fields.answer: No. Training bootstrap confidence-attenuates and detaches feedback. Inference uses unweighted pC and no extra bootstrap. Training heuristics are not posterior guarantees.
fields.example: Do not discount inference probability mass a second time because training suppressed low-confidence feedback.

fields.question: Why initialize calibration aψ to one and constrain it to [0.5,2]?
fields.answer: One preserves initial shortcut scale. Bounded exponential calibration avoids extreme amplification or suppression, with 5000 warmup steps. Verify ranges and gradient paths.
fields.example: Large calibration outputs must not make the shortcut dominate the vocabulary head.

fields.question: Why can LoopSpec use intermediate loop predictions without an independent drafter?
fields.answer: Shallower loop states give cheap predictions and deeper computation verifies them. Pipelined residual proposals aim to overlap waiting. Actual acceptance and scheduling determine gains; a reference scheduler does not measure GPU throughput.
fields.example: Reusing shallow drafts saves a separate model but frequent rejection can erase benefits.

fields.question: Why is self-speculation natural for shared-block loops?
fields.answer: Intermediate depth provides draft predictions and deeper loops verify. This reuses model weights; pipelined residual proposals reduce intended waiting.
fields.example: Draft with fewer loops, then verify with more.

fields.question: What does LoopSpec reuse compared with an independent drafter?
fields.answer: It reuses intermediate predictions and shared loop structure, rather than a second parameter set and path. Speed still depends on proposal quality, verification, and scheduling.
fields.example: Removing separate drafter weights does not ensure candidates are accepted.

fields.question: Does a depth scheduler establish real GPU pipelining?
fields.answer: No. It checks proposal/depth transitions, not actual overlap, cache handoff, or verification execution. Planned concurrency is not measured throughput.
fields.example: A log claiming overlap cannot show synchronization did not serialize the GPU.

fields.question: Why verify a candidate tree rather than concatenate each Medusa head's top token?
fields.answer: Heads predict different offsets from the same state and may not form a valid autoregressive chain. A tree exposes combinations for backbone validation. Independent losses do not prove correctness or sampling guarantees, and local work has no GPU tree kernel.
fields.example: Separately chosen nouns and verbs need not form a coherent phrase.

fields.question: Why add multiple future-token heads to one hidden state?
fields.answer: Different offsets provide multiple proposals at once. Tree verification can reduce sequential calls without removing backbone verification.
fields.example: Propose t+1 and t+2 from h_t before checking accepted combinations.

fields.question: Why don't fewer backbone calls imply the same percentage latency reduction?
fields.answer: Extra heads, tree construction and validation, batch shape, kernels, and acceptance all matter. Mechanism call counts are not measured GPU speed.
fields.example: Halving calls may double the work per verification.

fields.question: How align Medusa's k-th head targets?
fields.answer: Predict x_{t+k} from h_t, matching slices and valid endpoints. One common next-token target would train duplicate offsets.
fields.example: Head two at h_10 predicts x_12, not x_11.

fields.question: Why propagate gradients across several PUMBA carry steps?
fields.answer: Carry affects future denoising, so isolated loss may not learn useful carry. Unroll on-policy reveals and backpropagate within fixed windows, truncating between windows for cost. Local work is not full diffusion LM training.
fields.example: Later fill-in errors should shape how earlier carry represents entity constraints.

fields.question: Why train on the model's own progressive-unmasking trajectory?
fields.answer: Independent noise may miss states reached by actual multistep sampling. Carry through self-generated unrolls exposes dependent decisions.
fields.example: Revealed words determine the next input rather than independently recreating noise.

fields.question: How does trajectory-aware carry training differ from independent steps?
fields.answer: BPTT lets later loss affect earlier carry. Independent examples cut those dependencies, and summing their CEs does not restore them.
fields.example: Step-two loss should influence step-one carry, not only local step-two computation.

fields.question: Should PUMBA detach carry every step or at window boundaries?
fields.answer: Keep gradients through the fixed window and detach between windows. Per-step detachment removes the mechanism; fully untruncated training changes memory and protocol. Local reference did not train LLaDA-8B.
fields.example: At window length three, step three reaches two earlier steps in the same window only.

fields.question: Why align retrieval sets before compiling into a diffusion fan-out retriever?
fields.answer: Set value includes coverage and diversity beyond item relevance. Define trade-offs with a composite set reward, then train fast diffusion retrieval to approximate it. Reward alignment may be imperfect; local work only implements the set objective.
fields.example: Three individually relevant duplicates can be worse than a set covering separate facts.

fields.question: Why build a set-level alignment target before training a fast retriever?
fields.answer: Item scores alone may not guarantee whole-set properties. Compile a composite set target into diffusion fan-out to seek fewer online steps.
fields.example: Relevant outputs should cover different evidence rather than repeating one top item.

fields.question: How does set alignment differ from independent item ranking?
fields.answer: Sets account for relations and redundancy. Summing independent scores can miss coverage. The compiled retriever requires separate training and evaluation.
fields.example: Three high-relevance duplicates can have low diversity.

fields.question: Does the local R4T component train the 53.9M diffusion retriever?
fields.answer: No. It computes the alignment/diversity objective, without training the full generator. Scoring candidates is not generating fan-out results.
fields.example: A function ranking supplied sets cannot necessarily retrieve a set from a query.
